title: Installer key hardening (from the R4 security review)
why: R4's review found that the installer's own key store (installer/src/keys.rs), which /hub/install drives through `minerva keys`, can be made to trust a key again after it was revoked, and a few smaller gaps. The update keys are the trust root of `minerva update`, so this slice closes them in the installer itself. The findings are in I2-findings.md: arm-2 and arm-5 belong here. process-beside-overrides-flag and process-fake-misstates-real-remove were already closed in R4's merge (d8c5353); skip them.
owns_files: installer/src/*.rs (clippy-only changes, plus the callers of the keys API)
bin/hoot (arm-5 only, if the verb lives there)
tests:
- A revoked key's bytes re-added by hand under a fresh id are refused, and so is a rotation carrying them.
- trusted() never lists a key whose fingerprint is revoked.
- add_manual refuses an existing id with the same bytes, and a fingerprint under another id.
- A rotation key's meta is unchanged after any add_manual.
- ensure_dir: simulate a crash between steps (a leftover temp dir, a missing state.json) and check the next run neither trusts nothing nor everything.
- keys list --json error shape.
- The Nix allow-web sentence, with nothing armed.
- perch/tests/install.rs still passes against fake_minerva. The perch's contract with minerva is unchanged; if it must change, STOP and report.
live_check: None against the operator's install. Run every test under a temp HOME with MINERVA_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in it.
risk: This is the trust root of updates. A bug that refuses everything is safe; a bug that trusts a revoked key is not. Fail closed. Never run the real `minerva update`, never touch the real prefix or ~/.config/minerva.
